name: UT-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a +21 R lean
Incumbent Celeste Maloy running with large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at 4-5%

model.rationale: The district's heavy Republican lean, Maloy's incumbency and roughly 30-to-1 fundraising advantage, and markets pricing Democratic odds near 5% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. No polls or ratings suggest any reason to move off the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late scandal or major outside spending surge against Maloy could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Utah's 3rd District is a deeply Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Celeste Maloy is running for reelection and holds a decisive financial edge, having raised roughly $1.45 million plus outside support, while Democrat Kent Udell has raised under $50,000 with no outside backing. Minor-party and independent candidates trail far behind in resources.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket give Democrats only a 4-5% chance of an upset, and no expert ratings or general-election polls flag the race as competitive. The fundamentals, money, and market pricing all align on a Republican hold with a margin near 19 points.
